newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Securum says to pay 6.3 bln SKR to Sweden in '97.
newsitem.headline: Securum says to pay 6.3 bln SKR to Sweden in '97.

text.p: Securum, the company set up by the Swedish state to take over banks' bad debts in the early 1990s, said on Tuesday that it would give the state a dividend of 6.3 billion crowns in 1997.
Securum said it would hand over its remaining capital of about five billion crowns to the state in 1998.
Sweden's Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Tuesday that the state is to wind up Securum and transfer some of its remaining assets to state property company Vasakronan.
Vasakronan will get, at the most, two billion crowns, Securum said in a statement.

A small portfolio with remaining credits and a number of undertakings and follow up tasks will be transferred to Venantius AB, a company which also was set up by the state to take over bad debts in connection with the banking crisis.
All assets will have been transferred after the summer of 1997, the company said.
The government injected a total of 27.8 billion crowns into Securum and fellow company Retriva when they were created.
Retriva paid back its part, 3.8 billion crowns, when Securum took it over in the spring of 1996.
On top of that, Securum will be able to pay back more than 13 billion crowns when it is closed.
